audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagree on all seven rows: full has Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Kassadin/Kassadin while content has Ahri on every row.
audit.why: Kassadin's pre-6 kit is a 650-range Null Sphere and a 21s Force Pulse — Ahri clearly wins levels 1-5. After first and second item Riftwalk's cooldown falls to 3.5s and 2s and he chooses every engagement, which is what the full layer's 7/10 and 8/10 ratings already encode.
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side = Ahri (matching win[0..4]); win[5] and win[6] = Kassadin (matching phases[5..6].side already on disk). Chart proposed as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why and phases[6].why describe Ahri spikes while the side on those rows is Kassadin — the page tells the reader Kassadin wins and then explains why Ahri does.
audit.why: Kassadin's real spike is his mana/Sheen item, after which repeat Riftwalks stop being a liability.
audit.corrected: Rewrote both whys to Kassadin's item spike and his 2s Riftwalk.
sources: enemyKit R text on stacking mana cost

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction is absent: Void Stone reduces magic damage, and Ahri's Orb of Deception deals TRUE damage on the return — the half that ignores it, and ignores Null Sphere's magic shield too. Also spikes[0].text asserts Kassadin has "no shield yet" on Null Sphere, which contradicts Riot's own text.
audit.why: Riot text, Q: "The excess energy forms around himself, granting a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage." Passive: "Kassadin takes reduced magic damage and ignores unit collision." Ahri Q: "magic damage on the way out and true damage on the way back."
audit.corrected: Poke with the orb's return half; the true damage cuts through both Void Stone and the Null Sphere shield. Void Stone's collision-ignore also means minions never body-block his approach.

audit.whatIsWrong: Force Pulse's charging mechanic was never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot text: "Kassadin draws energy from spells cast in his vicinity." Your own Q, W and E cast near him arm his 21/20/19/18/17s slow.

audit.whatIsWrong: missingInteractions claims "Null Sphere (Q) is a channel — your Charm (E) cancels it outright." That is a derived-flag misfire.
audit.why: Riot's description says Null Sphere "interrupt[s] channels" — it is the interrupter, not a channel. Per the brief's own rule, the description wins over the flag.
audit.corrected: Not written to the page. The Nether Blade (W) auto-attack reset as a burst tell is genuine and is reflected in the trading lines.

edits.after: Kassadin wins by surviving to two items, where a 2-second Riftwalk lets him choose the fight and blink straight out of your Spirit Rush.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Count it out loud if you must. - Your R Spirit Rush (last dash) has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Riftwalk, 5/3.5/2s, 500 range: cheap on cooldown but each repeat blink costs more mana — the second one in a row is what he cannot afford early. - Force Pulse, 21s at rank 1, charges off spells cast near him, so every orb you throw beside him arms his slow.

edits.before: If Kassadin takes first blood, tighten up: Riftwalk is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with Q clears and stay relevant through charm picks.
edits.after: If Kassadin takes first blood he buys his mana items early and the lane clock flips: farm with Q, refuse the solo kill, and shove so every Riftwalk roam costs him CS. Stay relevant through flank Charms.

edits.before: Carry through picks — a landed charm is a won fight, and your dashes manufacture charm angles no one wards against.
edits.after: Carry through picks — punish the landing, not the blink: he arrives at 500 range and has to stand there, and Charm ends that.

edits.before: His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Riftwalk is 500 range and costs more each cast — Charm him on the landing, not on the approach.

edits.before: Q through his last-hit so both hits land, W if he eats the return, and walk — repeat until the charm window is lethal instead of optimistic.
edits.after: Riftwalk drops to a 2-second blink late, so the dash you bank is the only reason he doesn't get a free re-entry after you spend your rotation on him.

edits.before: Kassadin whiffs Riftwalk and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Null Sphere is 650 range — sit at 900 and he has to walk to you.

edits.before: That is Kassadin’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.

edits.before: Charming on cooldown for chip damage and then facing his real engage with nothing — the charm is the matchup, not the poke.
edits.after: Void Stone ignores unit collision, so minions never body-block his approach — never be caught past the river with Charm down.

edits.before: Track Kassadin’s Riftwalk: His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Riftwalk, 5/3.5/2s at 500 range: repeat blinks cost extra mana early. Your Q's return half is true damage — Void Stone can't stop it.

edits.before: Commit on Riftwalk’s cooldown, on your Malignance spike, and with your jungler’s setup. His answer goes first; yours goes last.
edits.after: Commit before he can afford a second Riftwalk, on your Malignance spike, and with your jungler's setup. Make him blink first, then Charm.

edits.before: Kassadin is one of the weakest laners in the game before 6 — no shield yet on Null Sphere's silence-and-poke, and Riftwalk isn't spammable, so you freely poke him with Orb of Deception and punish any farming attempt with Charm.
edits.after: Kassadin is one of the weakest laners before 6, but Null Sphere already grants a magic-damage shield — Orb of Deception's return half is true damage and ignores both that shield and Void Stone, so poke with the way back, not the way out.

edits.before: Kassadin has one of the worst level 1-2 kits in mid lane — Null Sphere is just a silence-poke on a long cooldown with no shield, so you freely win extended trades and can punish any CS attempt with Charm into full combo.
edits.after: Kassadin's level 1-2 is among the worst in mid, but Null Sphere does shield against magic — lean on Orb of Deception's return half, whose true damage cuts through both that shield and Void Stone's magic reduction.

edits.before: Kassadin scales his mobility but never his raw damage output — your Charm-locked burst combo still kills him faster than his Riftwalk blinks can punish, so you stay ahead through the skirmish phase if you keep landing Charm first.
edits.after: Kassadin scales past you: at two items Riftwalk is a 2-second blink he can pay for, so he chooses every engagement. Your late game is the flank Charm on someone he isn't guarding — arrive, pick, and leave before he lands.

edits.before: Full Riftwalk uptime still can't out-damage your itemized combo — you keep winning the fight.
edits.after: With a mana item Riftwalk hits 3.5s — he can blink in, commit, and blink out of your rotation.

edits.before: Even with infinite Riftwalk resets his mana-hungry blink pattern never out-trades your Charm-locked burst.
edits.after: At rank 3 Riftwalk is a 2-second blink he can afford — he picks the fight, so save Charm for the one aimed at you.

notes: Both layers of the level chart were wrong and in opposite directions — full read Skill on rows 0-4, content read Ahri on rows 5-6 while full read Kassadin there. Proposed the full flips and the two content flips together as the chart group. spikes[0].text's claim that Null Sphere has "no shield" contradicts Riot's own text and is corrected. The missingInteractions entry "Null Sphere is a channel — Charm cancels it" is a derived-flag misfire (Null Sphere interrupts channels; it is not one) and was NOT written to the page. Nether Blade's auto-reset is a real burst tell but there was no length-neutral field left to carry it without displacing better content — recorded here.
